hit.text: Kestrel Group Life Assurance pays a lump sum to a member's nominated beneficiaries if the member dies while covered under a participating employer's scheme. Cover is provided under a group policy issued to the employer or retirement fund.

hit.text:

question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?

result.question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?
result.answer: A member who leaves the employer before normal retirement age can apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age may apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.
citations.supports: The 60-day deadline to apply, the no-medical-evidence condition, and the cap of the lower of group cover and R5 000 000.
citations.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: The continuation rule is from the 2026 Group Life Product Guide (current edition). The documents do not say how the 60 days is counted beyond 'received within 60 days of leaving service'. Whether a specific member qualifies is decided by the claims or underwriting team.

question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?

result.question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?
result.answer: Under Option C, a member earning R50 000 a month would receive R42 500 a month. This is 100% of the first R20 000 of salary, plus 75% of the remaining R30 000. This is subject to the Option C maximum monthly benefit of R300 000, which this amount is below. The benefit starts after a 3-month waiting period. This is an illustration of the general rule; the claims team decides individual claims.

question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?

result.question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?
result.answer: The Kestrel Group Disability Income Benefit is paid monthly in arrears until the earliest of: the member's recovery, the member's death, or the member reaching age 65. So the benefit is paid up to age 65, unless the member recovers or dies earlier.

citations.title: Group Disability Income Benefit Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: The answer comes from the 2026 edition of the Group Disability Income Guide, which is the current edition in the documents.

question: Is there a waiting period on extended family funeral cover?

question: How many extended family members can be added to funeral cover, and what is the maximum entry age?

result.question: How many extended family members can be added to funeral cover, and what is the maximum entry age?
result.answer: A member can add up to 8 extended family members to funeral cover, such as parents, parents-in-law, siblings and grandparents. The maximum entry age for extended family members is 85. Each extended family member is insured for R10 000, and this cover is optional and paid for by the member through payroll deduction. A 6-month waiting period applies to death from natural causes for extended family members; death from accidental causes is covered immediately.

question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?

result.question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?
result.answer: To submit a disability claim, the member needs to provide: a completed Kestrel disability claim form (with both the employer section and the member section filled in), a medical report from the treating doctor, the member's last 3 payslips, and a certified copy of the member's ID document. Claims can be sent by the employer or broker through the Kestrel Broker Portal, or by email to claims@kestrel-assurance.example. Claims should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period. Disability claims may take longer to assess than group life claims, because medical information may need to be obtained.

question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?

result.question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?
result.answer: Kestrel aims to make a decision on a group life claim within 10 working days of receiving all required documents. This is a target, counted from when Kestrel has all the required documents. The claim is not decided on this timeline until the documents are complete.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: Kestrel aims to make a decision on group life claims within 10 working days of receiving all required documents.
citations.supports: The 10 working day target for a group life claim decision, counted from receipt of all required documents.
citations.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
citations.locator: section "How long does it take to assess a claim?"

citations.label: c2
citations.quote: The death of a member must be notified to Kestrel within 6 months of the date of death. Claims notified later may be declined.
citations.supports: The notification deadline caveat: the death must be notified within 6 months, or the claim may be declined.
citations.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: The 10 working days is an aim, not a guaranteed time. The clock starts only once all required documents have been received.
Disability claims may take longer because medical information may need to be obtained, so this timeline does not apply to them.
The death must be notified to Kestrel within 6 months of the date of death, or the claim may be declined (c2).

question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?

result.question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?
result.answer: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age has 60 days from leaving service to apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service, and no medical evidence is needed. The cover is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000. So the most they can continue is R5 000 000, or less if their group cover is lower.

question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?

result.question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?
result.answer: Under Option C, a member earning R50 000 a month would receive R42 500 a month. This is worked out as 100% of the first R20 000 of salary (R20 000), plus 75% of the balance above R20 000 (75% of R30 000 = R22 500). The benefit is capped at R300 000 a month, so this amount is within the cap. This is an illustration of the general rule, not a decision on any individual member's claim; the claims team decides individual cases.

question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?

result.question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?
result.answer: The Kestrel Group Disability Income Benefit is paid monthly in arrears until the earliest of three events: the member recovers, the member dies, or the member reaches age 65. So the benefit is paid up to age 65, unless it stops earlier because of recovery or death.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: The benefit is paid monthly in arrears until the earliest of: the member's recovery, the member's death, or the member reaching age 65.
citations.supports: The benefit is paid until the earliest of recovery, death, or age 65, so age 65 is the upper age limit.
citations.title: Group Disability Income Benefit Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: This is the general rule from the 2026 Group Disability Income Guide (current edition). Individual claims are decided by the claims team.

question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?

result.question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?
result.answer: To submit a disability claim, Kestrel needs these documents: the completed Kestrel disability claim form (with both the employer section and the member section), a medical report from the treating doctor, the member's last 3 payslips, and a certified copy of the member's ID document. The claim should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period. Claims can be sent by the employer or broker through the Broker Portal, or by email to claims@kestrel-assurance.example.

question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?

result.question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?
result.answer: Kestrel aims to make a decision on a group life claim within 10 working days of receiving all required documents. The clock starts only once all the documents are in. This is a target, not a guaranteed time. Also, the death must be notified to Kestrel within 6 months of the date of death, or the claim may be declined.

question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?

result.question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?
result.answer: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age can apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age may apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.
citations.supports: The 60-day application deadline, the no-medical-evidence condition, and the cap of the lower of group cover and R5 000 000.

caveats: The continuation rule is in the 2026 Group Life Product Guide, the only edition shown. The cap is the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000, so a member with less group cover than that gets less. The documents do not say whether the 60 days is counted from a different date in other cases; confirm edge cases with the scheme administrator or claims team.

question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?

result.question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?
result.answer: Under Option C, a member earning R50 000 a month would receive R42 500 a month. This is 100% of the first R20 000 of monthly salary, plus 75% of the balance, subject to the R300 000 monthly maximum. The waiting period is 3 months. This is an illustration of the rule using the figure given, not a decision on any individual claim; the claims team decides individual cases.

question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?

result.question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?
result.answer: The Kestrel group disability income benefit is paid monthly in arrears until the earliest of three events: the member recovers, the member dies, or the member reaches age 65. So the benefit stops at age 65 at the latest, unless the member recovers or dies earlier.

question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?

result.question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?
result.answer: For a disability claim, the documents needed are: the completed Kestrel disability claim form (with both the employer section and the member section), a medical report from the treating doctor, the member's last 3 payslips, and a certified copy of the member's ID document. The claim should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period. Claims can be sent through the Kestrel Broker Portal or by email to claims@kestrel-assurance.example. Disability claims may take longer to assess than group life claims because medical information may need to be obtained.

question: What is the premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members?

result.question: What is the premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members?
result.answer: The documents I can access do not state a premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members. The group life product guide says premiums are set as a percentage of the total annual salary bill of covered members, not as a rate per R1 000 of cover. The cover limit table shows the free cover limit for a 150-member scheme (R3 500 000), but that is a limit on free cover, not a premium rate. Please ask your broker or the scheme administrator for the current premium rate for a 150-member scheme.
result.reason: The documents do not state a premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for any scheme size. Please ask the broker or scheme administrator for the rate that applies to a 150-member scheme.

question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?

result.question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?
result.answer: Kestrel aims to make a decision on a group life claim within 10 working days of receiving all required documents. The 10 working days start only once all the required documents have been received.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: Kestrel aims to make a decision on group life claims within 10 working days of receiving all required documents.
citations.supports: Kestrel's target for deciding a group life claim is 10 working days after all required documents are received.
citations.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
citations.locator: section "How long does it take to assess a claim?"

citations.label: c2
citations.quote: The death of a member must be notified to Kestrel within 6 months of the date of death. Claims notified later may be declined.
citations.supports: The death must be notified to Kestrel within the stated period, or the claim may be declined.
citations.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: This is a target ('aims to'), not a guaranteed time. The documents do not say what happens if the claim is delayed. Claims are assessed by the claims team, which decides individual cases.

issues.detail: Before repair: The number 6 in the caveats comes from c2, which is not cited. Add a citation to c2 quoting the words that contain it.

hit.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
hit.locator: section "How long does it take to assess a claim?"
heading_path: How long does it take to assess a claim?
hit.text: Kestrel aims to make a decision on group life claims within 10 working days of receiving all required documents. Disability claims may take longer because medical information may need to be obtained. Funeral claims are paid within 48 hours of receiving complete documents.

hit.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
hit.text: The death of a member must be notified to Kestrel within 6 months of the date of death. Claims notified later may be declined. See the Kestrel Claims FAQ for the documents required.

hit.title: Group Funeral Benefit Scheme Rules (Version 2026.1)
hit.text: Funeral claims are paid within 48 hours of Kestrel receiving all the required documents.

hit.title: Group Disability Income Benefit Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
heading_path: Group Disability Income Benefit: Product Guide
hit.text: Claims should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period. See the Kestrel Claims FAQ for the documents required.

hit.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
hit.locator: section "What if I am unhappy with a claim decision?"
heading_path: What if I am unhappy with a claim decision?
hit.text: You can ask for the decision to be reviewed by writing to complaints@kestrel-assurance.example within 90 days of the decision. If you are still not satisfied, you may refer the matter to the long-term insurance ombud.
